newsitem.title: USA: UAL reaches tentative wage pact with pilots.
newsitem.headline: UAL reaches tentative wage pact with pilots.

text.p: UAL Corp. said Wednesday its United Airlines unit reached a tentative agreement with its 8,500 pilots, which includes four wage increases through the year 2000.

Under the agreement, the pilots represented by the Air Line Pilots Association would receive wage increases of 3 percent in both 1997 and 1998 and an additional 2 percent in both 1999 and 2000, UAL said.
Pilots will also be eligible for lump-sum profit-sharing payments in 1998 and 1999 based on the carrier's performance in the next two years, the airline said.
ALPA members will vote on the proposal in December.

"United's and ALPA's negotiators worked long and hard to reach an agreement that successfully balances the interests of United stockholders, our employees and our need to keep costs competitive," said UAL Chairman Gerald Greenwald.

The wage negotiation was built into UAL's 1994 employee stock ownership plan agreement with ALPA. At that time, the pilots union agreed to wage cuts and work rule changes in exchange for a stake in the airline.
The International Association of Machinists and salaried employees at UAL also gained a stake in the company in exchange for concessions.
Results of the ALPA vote are expected in mid-January.
